answer: An agent economy can starve grading farms by hiding decoy answers in every grading panel. Vetted authors write decoys with known scores, and the protocol feeds them through the same inlet as real answers, so graders cannot tell them apart. At close, auditors compute each grader's delta, the gap between its scores and the known ones. A delta above 1 zeroes that key's share of the grading nectar for three epochs. Panels differ per key, so 1,000 clone graders must each read their own queue honestly; one lazy script fails on all at once. Weakness: decoys need constant refreshing.
